samples.summary: The paste sanitizer bypasses every new numeric band — pasted lineHeight / fontSize / cell padding / rowHeights / image size still enter the model raw
samples.evidence: The diff bands these values at the two CRDT read boundaries (`model/crdt-tree.ts`, `frontend/.../yorkie-doc-store.ts`) and at `crdt-attrs.parseBlockStyleAttrs`. The clipboard parser is a third producer of the very same fields and passes none of them through the new normalizers: `sanitizeBlockStyle` accepts any finite `lineHeight` (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:183-189), `sanitizeInlineStyle` any finite `fontSize` (clipboard.ts:141-144), `sanitizeCellStyle` any finite `padding` (clipboard.ts:234-235), `sanitizeTableData` any finite `rowHeights` entry (clipboard.ts:296-298) and any finite image `width`/`height` (clipboard.ts:113-114) — while it *does* clamp `listLevel` (clipboard.ts:348-351), showing the ceiling was considered only for that one field. A payload on the system clipboard (the internal docs JSON MIME, or `text/html` with a `font-size` style) therefore lands a `1e9` line height / font size / padding in the local in-memory document and is then written back to the CRDT; the new `table-layout.ts` and `pagination.ts` bounds mitigate the table-row hang, but a non-table block's geometry (`assignLineHeights`, `totalHeight`, scroll extent) is still built from the raw value. `table-layout.ts:250-253`'s own comment acknowledges the gap ("the paste path (`sanitizeTableData`) admits any finite number") without closing it. The fix belongs in clipboard.ts's sanitizers (call `normalizeLineHeight`/`normalizeFontSize`/`normalizeCellPadding`/`normalizeRowHeight`/`isPaintableImageSize`), not in the new module.

samples.summary: The v1 docs-content PUT validator still accepts values the reader now silently rewrites, contradicting its own documented contract and breaking PUT→GET round-trip
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` accepts any finite number for every `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS` entry, including `lineHeight` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:399-407), and nothing in the walker validates inline `fontSize`, cell `padding`, `tableData.rowHeights` or `listLevel` at all. The GET path reads back through `@wafflebase/docs`'s `docsTreeToDocument` / `treeNodeToBlock` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:244), which this change makes drop or clamp those same values. So `PUT {lineHeight: 50}` / `{fontSize: 1000}` / `{listLevel: 40}` / `{rowHeights:[1e9]}` now returns 200 and a later GET returns the default or the band edge — exactly the behaviour the validator's own doc comment says it exists to prevent ("its job is to hand the caller a 400 instead of silently rewriting their style", docs-content.controller.ts:350-353). Either the validator should reject out-of-band values with a 400, or that comment and the API docs need updating.

samples.summary: Interactive row-resize writes row heights above the new MAX_ROW_HEIGHT ceiling, so the stored value and the laid-out value diverge
samples.evidence: `onDragMove` computes `newHeight = Math.max(currentHeight + deltaPx, 20)` and calls `this.doc.setRowHeight(...)` with no ceiling (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2227-2229); `Doc.setRowHeight` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:1180-1184) stores it verbatim. `computeTableLayout` now clamps the stored value through `normalizeRowHeight` (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:253), so a row dragged past `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT` (10000) stops growing on screen while the CRDT keeps the larger number, and the next drag restarts from the clamped layout height — a small but real drift between model and view introduced by the new band. Reachable only with an extreme drag, hence minor.

samples.summary: `normalizeRowHeights` (plural) is exported with no caller and is not re-exported from either package entry
samples.evidence: A repo-wide grep for `normalizeRowHeights` matches only its definition at packages/docs/src/model/row-height.ts:42; neither `packages/docs/src/index.ts:95` nor `packages/docs/src/node.ts:135` re-exports it (both export only `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT` / `normalizeRowHeight`). Dead export; knip's unused-export lane would flag it.

finding.summary: The paste sanitizer bypasses every new numeric band — pasted lineHeight / fontSize / cell padding / rowHeights / image size still enter the model raw

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate at every cited location. clipboard.ts's sanitizers use bare `asNumber` (clipboard.ts:69-71), which admits any finite value, for image width/height (113-114), fontSize (141-145), lineHeight (183-189), cell padding (234-235) and rowHeights (296-299); the file imports no normalizer from model/numeric-attrs.js or model/row-height.js and clamps only listLevel (7, 348-351). The new bands those fields are supposed to satisfy exist in model/numeric-attrs.ts:60-111 and are applied at crdt-tree.ts:83,97,146,220, crdt-attrs.ts:149 and yorkie-doc-store.ts:200,217,323,474 — so the clipboard is a third producer of the same fields that bypasses the guard entirely. The path is reachable: text-editor.ts:1673-1712 reads the WAFFLEDOCS_MIME payload off the system clipboard and hands the sanitized blocks to applyPastePlan/insertBlocks (1527, 4285, 4389). The "readers re-band it anyway" mitigation does not hold universally: Document refreshes from store.getDocument() (document.ts:129,148) and MemDocStore (store/memory.ts:43-45) performs no normalization at all, and it backs the TextEditor created in text-box-editor.ts:437,674 and the default editor in editor.ts:1045; on that path the raw multiplier flows into assignLineHeights (layout.ts:874-888), which floors at 1 but has no ceiling. table-layout.ts:246-253 documents the gap in-tree ("the paste path (`sanitizeTableData`) admits any finite number") and closes it only for rowHeights. This is a new-guard-with-a-bypass in the blast-radius lane, major per the rubric.
